title: Complexes with cohomology in a single degree
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $T$ be a separated
finite-type $k$-scheme, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ and let
$r\in\mathbf Z$.

1. *concentration in one degree.* If the
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] cohomology sheaves
$\mathcal H^i(K)$ vanish for every $i\neq r$, then the
truncation triangles induce a canonical isomorphism
$$
K\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;\mathcal H^r(K)[-r].
$$
1. *local constancy detected on an etale cover.* Let
$u:U\to T$ be a surjective
etale morphism and suppose
that $Lu^*K\cong\underline L[-r]$ for a
locally constant
$\Lambda$-sheaf $\underline L$ with finite stalks on $U$.
Then $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for every $i\neq r$, and
$\mathcal H^r(K)$ is locally constant with finite stalks on
$T$.

proof.text: The vanishing hypothesis makes K both IsGE r and IsLE r by the standard t-structure criteria. Apply Mathlib DerivedCategory.exists_iso_singleFunctor_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE, the declaration of [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single], to obtain e0 : K ≅ single_r(H'). Write H = H^r(K), E = singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso. The composite H' ≅ H^r(single_r(H')) ≅ H gives alpha; e1 = e0 followed by single_r(alpha) has H^r(e1) = E.inv at H by naturality and inverse cancellation. Compose with the inverse of singleFunctors.shiftIso (-r) r 0 to obtain the required normalized shift isomorphism.

If e is another normalized isomorphism, precompose e followed by the shift comparison with e0.inv. Fullness of single_r writes it as single_r(f); write e0.inv followed by e1 similarly as single_r(g). Naturality of E and the two normalization equalities give f = g. Cancel e0.inv and the shift comparison to conclude e = e1 followed by the inverse shift comparison. This proves uniqueness without choosing an unnormalized canonical map.

The ring in the purity setting is finite by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. A surjective etale map forms a singleton pro-etale cover by [lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover]. Use the exact constant-coefficient pullback functor and its additivity and finite-limit/colimit instances from [lem-pur-proetale-constant-module-pullback-homology] and [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Mathlib mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso identifies its value on H^i(K) with H^i of derived pullback. The supplied shift isomorphism then identifies this with H^i(single_r(L)), zero away from r and canonically L at r.

Apply restriction to constant scalars from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-encoding] and its pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-pullback-encoding]. Identify fixed-scalar upperStar with localized restriction, as in [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Covering conservativity, using the upstream isIso_of_isIso_localizationRestriction also underlying [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative], shows that the zero endomorphism of each H^i for i ≠ r is invertible after restriction to constant scalars. Hence that sheaf is zero. Faithfulness of restriction to constant scalars reflects its zero identity back to the intrinsic module sheaf.

In degree r the pullback is isomorphic to L. The finiteLocal_iff comparison proved in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-constructibility] identifies intrinsic local constancy with finite geometric stalks with the existence of a fixed-scalar pro-etale cover by finite constant module models. Transfer the cover of L across the pullback comparison and this isomorphism. Compose its members with u, using the composition axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The upperStarComp comparison trivializes H^r(K) on this composite cover. Apply finiteLocal_iff in the reverse direction to obtain intrinsic local constancy and finite geometric stalks on T. Empty schemes and empty covers are included, and no uniform finite bound or quasi-compactness of U is used.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions],
let $T$ be a separated
finite-type $k$-scheme, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ and let
$r\in\mathbf Z$.

1. *concentration in one degree.* If the
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] cohomology sheaves
$\mathcal H^i(K)$ vanish for every $i\neq r$, then the
truncation triangles induce a canonical isomorphism
$$
K\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;\mathcal H^r(K)[-r].
$$
1. *local constancy detected on an etale cover.* Let
$u:U\to T$ be a surjective
etale morphism and suppose
that $Lu^*K\cong\underline L[-r]$ for a
locally constant
$\Lambda$-sheaf $\underline L$ with finite stalks on $U$.
Then $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for every $i\neq r$, and
$\mathcal H^r(K)$ is locally constant with finite stalks on
$T$.

proof.text:
Step 1: the truncation triangles. By
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] the sheaves
$\mathcal H^i(K)$ are the cohomology sheaves for the standard
t-structure, and for every $a\in\mathbf Z$ there are exact triangles
$\tau_{\leq a-1}K\to\tau_{\leq a}K\to\mathcal H^a(K)[-a]\to$ and
$\tau_{\leq a}K\to K\to\tau_{\geq a+1}K\to$. A complex all of whose
cohomology sheaves vanish is zero in the derived category of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], that category being the
localization at the quasi-isomorphisms. If therefore
$\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for every $i\neq r$, then
$\tau_{\geq r+1}K\simeq0$ and $\tau_{\leq r-1}K\simeq0$, and the two
triangles exhibit $K$ and $\mathcal H^r(K)[-r]$ as models of one
and the same object; this is (1).
Step 2: an etale cover. Pullback of sheaves is exact, so the derived
pullback $Lu^*$ commutes with cohomology sheaves, and etale
morphisms are weakly etale, hence covering families in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] (an etale morphism is flat with
flat diagonal, which is the description of weakly etale in
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]); the description of etale
morphisms is that of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Since $u$ is a
member of a pro-etale covering family, inverse image along $u$
reflects vanishing of a sheaf, by clause (1) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative]; as $Lu^*K\cong \underline L[-r]$ has cohomology only in degree $r$, the sheaves
$u^*\mathcal H^i(K)\cong\mathcal H^i(Lu^*K)$ vanish for $i\neq r$,
and therefore so do the sheaves $\mathcal H^i(K)$. For the remaining
degree, $u^*\mathcal H^r(K)\cong\underline L$ is constant along the
covering $u$, so $\mathcal H^r(K)$ is locally constant in the sense
recalled in [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; the stalks of a
constructible object may be computed at geometric points, by part (3) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative], and they are the stalks of
$\underline L$ there, hence finite. This is (2).
